narrative: Material PL1__M890BCAD exhibits erratic demand patterns with an average daily consumption of 494 units and a coefficient of variation of 35.2%. The demand distribution is best characterized as Normal, with a slight declining trend over the observation period. Lead time performance shows volatile characteristics (CV=48.1%), with a mean of 1.15 days and standard deviation of 0.55 days. The effective lead time (mean + 1σ) is 1.70 days. The primary driver of inventory uncertainty is lead time variability, accounting for 68.1% of the total variance in lead time demand. This indicates that improving supplier reliability and reducing lead time fluctuations would yield the greatest risk reduction. The optimized policy recommends a safety stock of 543 units to achieve the target 95% service level, combined with an order quantity of 3755 units based on economic order quantity principles. This represents a reorder point of 1382 units, triggering replenishment when on-hand inventory reaches this threshold. Compared to the current SAP configuration (zero safety stock, MOQ-based ordering), the recommended policy delivers substantial cost savings of $9,852 annually (63.4% reduction) through optimized order frequency and improved service level protection.

research_insights.selection_rationale: The Normal distribution was selected based on empirical demand characteristics (CV=35.21%). Lead time demand variance incorporates both demand and lead time uncertainty using the standard propagation formula: σ²(LTD) = L·σ²(D) + D²·σ²(L). The 95% service level is achieved using z=1.645 from the standard normal distribution.
